units.text: Use this playbook when a Compose UI test fails on Robolectric and the cause is not known.
1. Run the failing test and record the exact command, the failure message, and the stack trace.
2. Print the semantics tree at any point in the test, because looking at it is the main way to solve problems in tests. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#semantics-tree-printing).

quotes.quote: The main way to solve problems in your tests is to look at the semantics tree. Print the tree by calling composeTestRule.onRoot().printToLog() at any point in your test.

units.text: 3. Print the semantics tree with `useUnmergedTree` set to true as well as the default tree, because some nodes merge the semantics information of their children. See [semantics-finders.md](../core/semantics-finders.md#merged-and-unmerged-trees).

quotes.quote: Some nodes merge the semantics information of their children.
If you need to match a node of what would be the unmerged tree, you can set useUnmergedTree to true

units.text: 4. Check whether the UI has identical Compose elements nested inside multiple traditional Android Views, where a standard Compose search might fail with a "Multiple nodes found" error. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#multiple-nodes-found-inside-android-views).

quotes.quote: When migrating complex UIs to Compose, you might encounter identical Compose elements nested inside multiple traditional Android Views
In these scenarios, a standard Compose search like onNodeWithText("Save") might fail with a "Multiple nodes found" error.

units.text: 5. If an assertion fails right after launching a task and the data is still in a "Loading" state, check whether the test uses the v2 APIs, which queue coroutines instead of executing them immediately. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#assertion-fails-after-launching-a-task-v2-apis).

quotes.quote: Failure: You launch a task (for example, a ViewModel loads data), but your assertion fails immediately because the data is still in a "Loading" state.
Cause: With the v2 APIs, coroutines are queued rather than executed immediately. The task was queued but never actually ran before the result was checked.

units.text: 6. If the UI does not update after a state change, check whether the test used the methods that synchronize it, because without them no recomposition occurs. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#ui-appears-paused).

quotes.quote: However, if you don't use the methods that synchronize your tests, no recomposition will occur and the UI will appear to be paused.

units.text: 7. If the failure mentions unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue, note that `LooperMode.PAUSED` warns when a test fails with them. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#looper-warnings).

quotes.quote: However, it has the following improvements: Robolectric will warn users if a test fails with unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue
LooperMode.PAUSED

units.text: 8. Check whether the test relies on a non-touch input mode configured through instrumentation APIs before the test starts, which can make tests fail during migration. See [flaky-tests.md](../debugging/flaky-tests.md#input-mode-leakage).

quotes.quote: Tests can fail during migration if they rely on non-touch input modes configured through instrumentation APIs before the test starts.

units.text: 9. If the project uses version 1.13 or later of ui-test, capture screenshots and UI hierarchies automatically upon test failure, because debugging UI tests often requires inspecting the screen state and composition hierarchy. See [debugging.md](../references/debugging/debugging.md#failure-artifacts).

quotes.quote: Debugging UI tests often requires inspecting the screen state and composition hierarchy when an assertion fails.
You can automatically capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon failure
The APIs associated with the failure handler pipeline (TestFailurePolicy, TestFailureHandler, and FailureContext) are included in androidx.compose.ui:ui-test:1.13.0-alpha01+
failurePolicy Cmn android Added in 1.13.0-rc01

units.text: 10. If it is not clear whether resources are loaded for a library, turn on Robolectric debug logging. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#debug-logging).

quotes.quote: If you are not sure if resources are being loaded for a particular library, enable debug logging by setting the system property robolectric.logging.enabled = true and run your tests.

units.text: 11. Use the Robolectric simulator to preview how your UI would look in a Robolectric environment, which can be helpful when debugging failing Robolectric tests. Report what it shows as a preview only, because it is highly experimental and still largely in the proof-of-concept stage, and UI rendered in it may not match an Android emulator or device 100%. See [debugging.md](../references/debugging/debugging.md#robolectric-simulator).

quotes.quote: This can be helpful, for instance, when debugging failing Robolectric tests.
UI rendered in the Robolectric simulator may not match an Android emulator or device 100%.
The Robolectric simulator can be a useful way to preview how your UI would look in a Robolectric environment.
Note that the Robolectric simulator is highly experimental and is still largely in the proof-of-concept stage.

units.text: 12. Check whether the failure comes from a documented difference between Android libcore and OpenJDK, or from a fidelity limit of Robolectric. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#android-libcore-and-openjdk-differences) and [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#fidelity-limits).

quotes.quote: Because of that, you may notice different behaviours when running your app on a device or emulator, and running your tests on the JVM with Robolectric.
Robolectric provides enough fidelity to run most UI tests but some cases will still require device tests

units.text: 13. If a rendering assertion fails after advancing the clock, check whether the test waited for the draw pass to complete. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#wait-for-draw-before-capturing).

quotes.quote: you want to assert anything related to rendering (e.g. SemanticsNodeInteraction.captureToImage), you will need a call to androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.ComposeTestRule.waitForIdle or androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.ComposeTestRule.runOnIdle to make sure that any triggered draw pass has been completed.

units.text: - State the cause as the first place the evidence shows the test going wrong, with the command output, file and line, or official page behind it.
- Separate what the evidence shows from what you infer.
- If no official page covers the behavior, say it is not documented.
- List open questions.
- Fix the cause the evidence points to, with the smallest change. Each item below applies to one cause from the investigation.

- Merged tree hides the node: set `useUnmergedTree` for a special need to inspect implementation detail within children. See [semantics-finders.md](../core/semantics-finders.md#merged-and-unmerged-trees).

quotes.quote: If you need to match a node of what would be the unmerged tree, you can set useUnmergedTree to true
useUnmergedTree is for tests with a special need to inspect implementation detail within children

units.text: - Identical elements inside Android Views: use `onRootWithViewInteraction`, which is experimental and subject to change. See [interoperability.md](../advanced/interoperability.md).

quotes.quote: Use the onRootWithViewInteraction API on your test rule. This function accepts an Espresso ViewInteraction
This API is experimental and subject to change.

units.text: - Queued coroutines: use `waitForIdle` or `runOnIdle` to execute queued tasks before asserting. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#assertion-fails-after-launching-a-task-v2-apis).

quotes.quote: Use waitForIdle or runOnIdle to execute queued tasks before asserting

units.text: - Condition that depends on external work: use `waitUntil`. See [synchronization.md](../core/synchronization.md#waiting-for-conditions).

quotes.quote: Any condition that depends on external work, such as data loading or Android's measure or draw (that is, measure or draw external to Compose), should use a more general concept such as waitUntil()

units.text: - Unexecuted main Looper tasks: if you see test failures like 'Main looper has queued unexecuted runnables.', insert `shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle()` calls into your test to drain the main Looper. See [synchronization.md](../references/core/synchronization.md#draining-the-main-looper).

quotes.quote: you may need to insert shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle() calls to your test to drain the main Looper
Main looper has queued unexecuted runnables.

units.text: - Non-touch input mode: specify the required input mode in `ComposeUiTestConfig`. See [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#input-mode).

quotes.quote: To resolve this, specify the required input mode in ComposeUiTestConfig

units.text: - Rendering assertion after advancing the clock: call `waitForIdle` or `runOnIdle` before asserting. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#wait-for-draw-before-capturing).

quotes.quote: you want to assert anything related to rendering (e.g. SemanticsNodeInteraction.captureToImage), you will need a call to androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.ComposeTestRule.waitForIdle or androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.ComposeTestRule.runOnIdle to make sure that any triggered draw pass has been completed.

units.text: - Rerun the failing test with the same command and record the result.
- Reintroduce the cause, confirm the test fails again, then restore the fix.
- Print the semantics tree again after the fix and compare it with the tree from the investigation. See [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#semantics-tree-printing).

quotes.quote: Print the tree by calling composeTestRule.onRoot().printToLog() at any point in your test.

units.text: - Remove temporary diagnostic output added during the investigation, and run the rest of the module's tests.
- Ask an independent reviewer for a different explanation that fits the same evidence.
- Delegate to one read-only subagent: run the failing test and capture its full output.
- Delegate to a second read-only subagent: read the code under test and the recent changes to it, and report what could produce the failure.
- Keep for yourself: printing the semantics tree, comparing the two reports, naming the cause, and making the fix.
- After verification, delegate the challenge to a fresh reviewer: look for a different cause that fits the same evidence.
- Change only what the named cause requires.
- Remove the temporary output and probes added while investigating.
